title: Quiet moves
line: A combination where the key move is not a check or a capture.

steps.text: Levitsky against Marshall, 1912: Black has a quiet move that leaves White lost whatever White does.
Put your queen on g3, where both white pawns and the white queen can capture her. No capture saves White.
steps.hint: The queen goes where two pawns and the white queen can all take her.
steps.after: Suppose the pawn on h2 takes the queen.
Checkmate: the rook on h3 and the knight leave the king no square.

steps.text: Now suppose the pawn on f2 takes instead. Check with the knight first.
steps.after: The king had to go to the corner.

steps.text: Last, suppose White's queen takes yours. Check with the knight.
Take the queen back, with check.
steps.after: Black has the queen back and is as far ahead as before. Levitsky saw all this and gave up the game.

summary: The strongest move is not always a check or a capture. A quiet move can leave every answer losing.
